findings.description: Critical: The Git-commit staleness rule can yield a negative age. design.md and spec.md define staleness_days as manifest as_of minus git log -1 --format=%cI for an unmodified tracked provenance path, but neither defines commit_time > as_of. Git committer dates may be future-dated, and host as_of may legitimately precede that timestamp; digest.schema.json requires staleness_days minimum 0, while feeding a negative value into min(floor(staleness_days/30), 5) would invert the penalty into a boost.
findings.resolution: Fail closed on clock skew: when commit_time > as_of, set staleness_days to null with an explicit degraded marker (preferred) or clamp to 0; never admit a negative value into the ranking formula. Add a task-1.3 fixture covering future committer dates.

findings.description: Critical: Crash-recoverable publication still does not cover lifecycle deletions. Revision 4 requires pre-SENSE maintenance to delete terminal stub/cache files and publish a rebuilt digest/mirror baseline, while the journal is defined only as replacement bytes/checksums for cache/digest/mirror targets with digest.json last. Spec.md further says only a wholly valid score document may create a journal and publish, which either forbids journaling the no-score maintenance path or forces unjournaled deletes. A crash after prune and before digest-last therefore leaves durable mixed state the stated roll-forward protocol cannot reconstruct; task 4.1 only interrupts after target replaces, not delete boundaries.
findings.resolution: Extend the transaction to encode replace and delete ops, include terminal stub/cache deletions with the rebuilt digest/mirror in one journal, clarify that cache-only maintenance may create that journal without a freshly dispatched score document, and add interruption tests at every deletion/replacement boundary.

findings.description: Nit: Digest Approval Routing still says the request SHALL place by stub priority unless --after overrides it, while the next sentences say explicit priority and insertion position are independent and no renumbering is implied. Refiner _apply_add preserves an explicit priority via setdefault and otherwise appends; an implementer can read the first clause as computing insertion from priority.
findings.resolution: Reword to: copy stub priority into the item; default insertion is append unless --after selects position; priority and position are independent.

findings.description: Revision 4 correctly splits generated_at from state_updated_at so cache-only lifecycle rebuilds preserve scoring evidence time, validate cached scored_at against generated_at, and still expose the later maintenance transition without dispatching a scorer.
findings.resolution: Keep the two-clock contract and the cache-only validation tests called out in tasks 1.3 and 1.4.

findings.description: The complete canonical prompt-manifest 64 KiB bound, per-artifact 2 KiB excerpt cap, oversized:<stub_key> fail-closed path, contained regular-file loader, sanitize_string redaction, and untrusted delimiters close the round-2 partial-bound gap without leaving a single schema-valid stub able to force an oversize dispatch.
findings.resolution: Preserve prepare-batch fail-before-dispatch behavior and the individually oversized stub fixtures in tasks 1.5 and 4.1.

findings.description: The approval-routing contract now matches refine-roadmap behavior: _apply_add never calls _renumber_priorities, setdefault preserves an explicit priority, and the plan no longer claims renumbering on add.
findings.resolution: Keep explicit priority copy plus independent --after insertion in stub-to-request tests.

findings.description: digest.schema.json weights now emit staleness_penalty_cap, risk_higher_is_safer, decision_bucket_order, dependency_bucket_order, and tie_breaker alongside the numeric weights, so a consumer can reconstruct the advertised total order from the artifact alone.
findings.resolution: Keep the expanded weights object required and const-constrained through contract installation.

findings.description: Ranking and stub-to-request now consistently build a strict all-status index from roadmap YAML, active changes, and archived changes with an explicit archived-completed rule, and both proposal and tasks forbid using ri-16 ready-frontier output as that index.
findings.resolution: Implement the shared index once and reuse it for dependency_ready and routing resolution as tasks 1.3 and 1.8 require.

findings.description: Failed scoring now has a coherent retry ledger rule: no journal or output updates, prior digest preserved, and the last successful cycle fingerprint left unadvanced so the unchanged early exit cannot suppress the next retry.
findings.resolution: Keep the unadvanced-fingerprint assertion in the scoring-failure and integration fixtures.

findings.description: FYI: proposal Impact still lists digest.py subcommands as store/rank/digest/stub-to-request/decide and omits prepare-batch, even though What Changes, design D3/D8, tasks, and the normative spec all make prepare-batch the public bounded-manifest boundary.
findings.resolution: Add prepare-batch to the Impact command list on the next editorial pass; behavior is already specified elsewhere.
